clues.text: This city began as a small village on the east bank of a creek. Wild salt marshes spread around it on the flat plains.
clues.narrowing: Points to a plains village site by a creek, ringed by salt marshes.

source.quote: The village was sited on the east bank of Salt Creek

clues.text: No sea or high land sits near to soften the weather here. So winters bite with hard cold, and summers hit with waves of heat.
clues.narrowing: Rules out mild coasts; keeps plains towns with hard swings of cold and heat.

source.quote: far from the moderating influences of mountains and large bodies of water, Lincoln has a highly variable four season humid continental climate

clues.text: In 1867, a state team toured new sites for the capital, far from the old seat. They picked this tiny salt marsh village to take the job.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to a tiny village picked as the new capital in 1867.

source.quote: The village of Lancaster was chosen, in part due to its salt flats and marshes.

clues.text: This town took a new name for President Abraham, who had just been shot dead. Some hoped that name would stop the move here, but it did not work.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital took the name of a slain president in 1867.

source.quote: Omaha Senator J. N. H. Patrick made a last-ditch effort to derail the move by having the future capital named after recently assassinated President Abraham Lincoln

clues.text: The governor of Nebraska works in this city. All the state lawmakers meet here to make laws.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and all state lawmakers work in this city.

source.quote: state capitol building was completed in 1932 and is the nation's second-tallest capitol

reveal.blurb: Founded in 1856 as a salt marsh village, this town was picked as the new capital in 1867 and renamed for a slain president. Its tall tower was done in 1932; the building is the capitol, and the city is the capital. Lincoln is the capital of Nebraska.
